note: He fails three of the five criteria as written. Good-to-great: he rates himself 4 out of 10 and is explicitly in recovery, not optimisation — 'I've been in fantastic shape in my life... and I'm not there.' Neglected health: his was a crisis, not neglect — a possible ankylosing spondylitis diagnosis, lab work, a year of counselling, and a period where he could not stand at a sink for five minutes. Not-deconditioned: this is the exclusion the stated ICP describes almost word for word — he peaked at 280 lb against a remembered 180, still carries 20-30 lb of fat, currently trains only bodyweight calisthenics, and accumulated 'I don't even know how many gym memberships, and with all the best intentions, but then just never found the time'. Successful holds: he supervises and trains others, has his own office and reports annual raises. Income is genuinely ambiguous and left unscored — good gross earnings but no discretionary liquidity ('the money's just going out the door, no matter how much I make, it's all gone') and a household spending freeze he himself imposed. This is a clear out-of-ICP prospect being sold at full price, and the criterion that should have stopped the call — whether the body can safely do loaded ballistic work — does not exist in the stated ICP at all.
